key_insight: Instead of using a single, fixed masking/corruption ratio for self-supervised time-series learning, treat the corruption level as a controllable degree of freedom and learn representations by modeling the entire corruption "flow" with a Flow-Guided Neural Operator (FGNO). This yields more flexible, robust representations across corruption levels.
problem_solved: Most SSL methods for time-series (e.g., MAE-style) rely on a predetermined, static masking/corruption ratio, which limits robustness, requires costly hyperparameter tuning, and can fail to capture multi-scale temporal dynamics.
method: Introduce FGNO: a neural-operator-style module that models mappings across a continuum of corruption levels (the "flow") rather than a single fixed mask.
Use self-supervised reconstruction / prediction objectives over corrupted-to-clean flows so the model learns representations stable across varying corruption strengths and time scales.
Train end-to-end with flow-guided sampling (varying corruption levels during training) to produce transferable, robust time-series embeddings without per-task masking tuning.
impact: FGNO reduces sensitivity to masking hyperparameters and produces flexible, robust time-series representations that transfer better across downstream tasks and corruption regimes, simplifying SSL pipelines for practitioners.
visual_elements: Schematic comparing static masking (single ratio) vs. flow-guided corruption (continuum) — arrow showing learned mapping across corruption levels.
Architecture block: FGNO module inserted between corrupted input and representation head, with icons for time-series, operator, and learned flow.
Performance chart: downstream accuracy/robustness vs. masking ratio showing FGNO maintaining high performance across a wide range versus baselines.
Timeline/flow diagram: sampling various corruption levels during training and producing a unified embedding space (illustrates curriculum/flow sampling).
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning via Flow-Guided Neural Operator on Time-Series Data
paper_authors: Duy Nguyen, Jiachen Yao, Jiayun Wang, Julius Berner, Animashree Anandkumar
